text.p: American Airlines Tuesday confirmed an order of seven Boeing 777-200IGW aircraft to be delivered in early 1999 and 2000.
The AMR Corp. subsidiary also confirmed purchase rights for additional 777s in late 1999, 2000 and 2001.
In November 1996, American agreed to buy aircraft exclusively from Boeing Co. in exchange for highly competitive prices and terms, the airline said.

Last month, American said, it finalised terms for firm orders and purchase rights for the 737, 757 and 767 aircraft that form the bulk of the aircraft order but deferred the 777 decision for further analysis of the various 777 models.
The airline said it selected the IGW -- for increased gross weight -- aircraft to replace the McDonnell Douglas Corp. MD-11s it plans to retire over the next five years.
The IGWs have greater range than the MD-11s and they will better position American for Pacific growth, the airline said.
IGWs are about the same size as the MD-11s.
American said the new aircraft will be configured with first class, business class and main cabin.
The airline said it has not selected engines for the 777.

Under the terms of its agreement with Boeing, American said, it can choose to expand the IGW fleet during the next few years. Longer term, it may choose to supplement the IGW fleet with new 777 variants as they become available.
American, based in Fort Worth, Texas, said it is particularly interested in a longer range model that will be able to fly nonstop routes of nearly 10,000 miles.
AMR's stock fell $5.75 to $93.75 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
